title: Every served read reaches a screen: the route roster, the forensic view, the design pass
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-e7a20a498ed0436380e5aca23cb81607 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-2ee775b319cb496fad9256c84d24744c, Resources) and child 2 (task-1c9587ed1b2b4e1abd6b51396ee672f8, the two dossiers) - the roster test only passes once their screens consume their reads. PROOF ROW: it owns the bidirectional roster, the Playwright journeys, the design pass and the live drive.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: (a) the bidirectional route roster test; (b) an 'Advanced' forensic view behind a toggle listing the remaining raw reads (events, work items) so nothing served is unreachable; (c) the design pass with the apple-design-skill and frontend-design skills; (d) the Playwright journeys and the live drive.

HOW TO ENUMERATE THE SERVED SET - measured, because the parent's instruction needs a technique. `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` (539 lines) contains NO literal route strings: it IMPORTS `*_READ_PATH` / `*_PATH` constants and dispatches on them (DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH :3, GOAL_CATALOG_READ_PATH :5, PLANNING_RUN_READ_PATH :9, PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_READ_PATH :11, DOCUMENT_COVERAGE_READ_PATH :25, RUNS_READ_PATH :27, POLICY_READ_PATH :29, ACTIVATION_READ_PATH :30, HEALTH_READ_PATH :31, ACTIVITY_READ_PATH :32, SESSIONS_READ_PATH :33, REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH :34, GOAL_SOURCE_READ_PATH :35, and more). So the served set is derived from those imported constants - NOT from a hand-kept list, which would be a third copy free to drift (global rail 9: enumerate from the implementation seam).

A GAP THIS TEST WILL CATCH, already known: `REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH` is served (:34) but has NO browser decoder and is absent from dev-proxy-paths.ts - see comment-81312c74 on task-19d2329c. task-e6000b57fd374f78ba074b9f0f0f2c67 is planned to add it. If that row has not landed when this test goes green-or-red, the honest outcome is a RED roster naming the unconsumed route - record it and coordinate; do NOT special-case the route to get a pass, because the whole point of the test is that it names exactly this class of gap.

DELIBERATELY UNCONSUMED, and must stay so: planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.*, work.* are unconnected BY DESIGN and stay forensic. The roster test must express that as an explicit, justified exclusion list with a reason per entry - not as a silent omission, or the test stops meaning anything.
definitionOfDone: A bidirectional roster test asserts SET EQUALITY (not subset, both directions) between the read routes the daemon SERVES - derived from the `*_PATH` constants http-listener-read-dispatch.ts imports and dispatches on, never a hand-kept list - and the routes the control-room client consumes. Deleting a consumer must red it, and adding a served route with no consumer must red it; verify both by doing them.

The deliberate exclusions (planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.*, work.*) are an EXPLICIT list with a stated reason per entry, asserted as exclusions rather than omitted - an exclusion list without reasons becomes a place to hide a real gap.

An 'Advanced' forensic view behind a toggle lists the remaining raw reads (events, work items) so nothing served is unreachable from the UI; a test asserts the toggle is off by default and that the view renders the raw frames when opened.

DESIGN PASS recorded in a row comment: the skills used (apple-design-skill, frontend-design), the findings, the fixes applied, and before/after screenshots from the live lane. The owner's ask was 'we need it for humans not bots' - a comment listing skills without naming what CHANGED does not discharge this.
Playwright journeys against a REAL daemon for Resources and the contract dossier, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted.

LIVE DRIVE on the lane (UnAI or a fresh project): transcript, store path and sha in a row comment under ~4500 chars. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT BUILD SCREENS. Resources is child 1's and the two dossiers are child 2's; if a screen is missing a fact the roster needs, comment on that child and report_blocked rather than adding it here.

NEVER SPECIAL-CASE A ROUTE TO GET THE ROSTER GREEN. An unconsumed served route is exactly what this test exists to name; a red roster naming REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH is a correct result, not a failure to work around.
ENUMERATE FROM THE SEAM, not from a constant: the served set comes from the paths the listener actually dispatches on. A hand-kept list is a third copy and drifts (global rail 9).
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description: BASELINE AND RE-MEASURE. Record, in the step note, the pre-change count lines for `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and for the targeted daemon roster leg `cd apps/daemon && npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` (expect 7 passed (7), exit 0). Then re-run the four consumption greps from planningNotes.codebaseInsights section C and paste their verbatim output, because a peer row may have closed one while this plan was being written. If a route has gained a consumer, drop it from the census before writing it. Do NOT edit any file in this step.

CONSUMER SCANNER plus the two new bidirectional arms, in the EXISTING asserter. In apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts add `consumedPaths()`: walk apps/control-room/src and packages/control-room-client/src for .ts/.tsx, SKIP any path containing `.test.` or ending dev-proxy-paths.ts, strip // and /* */ comments from each file (risk R2 - live-config.ts:81 and live-handshake.ts:38 name routes inside comments), and collect every `"/..."` literal. Then assert BOTH directions as sets, never subset: (a) JSON_ROUTES minus consumed == UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES; (b) consumed-and-daemon-shaped minus JSON_ROUTES == the permitted non-JSON_ROUTES surface already named at :182 (/bootstrap and the four /session/pair* paths). Direction (b) is what catches a browser fetching a route this daemon does not serve.

THE EXCLUSION CENSUS WITH A REASON PER ENTRY (DoD 2), and its positive control. Declare UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES as a frozen list where every entry carries a written reason in an adjacent comment - currently /events/resume (client-transport.ts declares page and ack but not resume; generated-client.ts:28 says resume semantics are TBD), /graph/get, /v2/product-contract/current (the browser consumes .../pending/read, not current) and /session/challenge-operands/read. An entry with no reason is a hiding place, so assert the reasons EXIST: pin that each census member's name appears in the file's comment block. Extend the existing positive-control arm at :189 with floors for the new scan (files walked > 100, consumed paths > 15) so no new arm can pass on an empty set. Then DRILL, per global rail 1: delete live-repository-remote.ts's route literal and confirm arm (a) reds naming /repository/remote/read; add a fake served route to JSON_ROUTES and confirm arm (a) reds; add a bogus "/not/served/read" literal to a control-room production module and confirm arm (b) reds. Restore all three and prove restoration with `git status --porcelain` on the exact paths in a SEPARATE call.

THE COMMAND-KIND EXCLUSIONS (DoD 2's named entries: planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.*, work.*). These are KINDS, not routes - they travel over /command and /v2/command. Enumerate the served kinds from the daemon seam (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts) and the browser-advertised kinds from packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts (builders declared per kind, e.g. :187 cutover.abort, :188 cutover.activate). Assert the deliberate exclusions as an EXPLICIT reasoned list rather than a silent omission, and state per entry which sense of unconsumed applies - note the measured subtlety that cutover.* IS advertised by the generated client while the UI gates it at approvals/approval-detail-confirmation.tsx:31, so 'not advertised' and 'not offered in the UI' are different claims and the census must not conflate them. If this enumeration proves to need more than the two seam files above, STOP and report rather than widening the file roster (global rail 19 - that is a split signal, not a discovery for step 8).

DECIDE /graph/get BEFORE BUILDING AGAINST IT (risk R4). Read serveGraphQuery at apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-command-stream-routes.ts:286 and record its request contract - method, body shape, whether it needs the CSRF token and projectId the handshake carries - in the step note. It sits in the UNGUARDED_MEMBERS census at http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:69-72, so it is NOT guaranteed to be a plain GET. Two outcomes, both legitimate: if the browser can consume it with the credentials it already holds, write apps/control-room/src/live/live-graph-get.ts as a thin exact-key-decoded port plus its test, and delete /graph/get from the census in the SAME edit. If consuming it would need new daemon bytes, task rail 1 forbids adding them here: leave it in the census with that measured reason recorded, and build the Advanced view against the raw event frames alone. Write which branch was taken and why.

THE ADVANCED FORENSIC VIEW (DoD 3), as its own module under the free `cr.advanced.*` testid namespace (measured free: 0 hits under apps/control-room/src and tests). New file apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/advanced-view.tsx, under 250 lines, ASCII-only, no apostrophes in any rendered string (task rail 4). It renders the remaining raw reads - the raw event frames, plus work items from the step-5 port if that branch was taken - as frames, not as prose summaries: the point is that a served read is reachable, so show what the daemon actually returned. Every frame goes through the PRODUCTION exact-key decoder, never a hand-written shape (task rail 4 of task-2ee775b3's precedent: a drifted fixture must red at the decode, not render a refusal silently).

ADVANCED VIEW TESTS plus the shell mount. New apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/advanced-view.test.tsx asserting exactly what DoD 3 names: the toggle is OFF BY DEFAULT (assert the rendered content is absent via queryByTestId returning null, not merely that a flag is false), and opening it RENDERS THE RAW FRAMES (assert on decoded frame content by exact string, not on the container existing). Add a refusal arm: when a raw read refuses, its code renders VERBATIM (global rail 1 - assert the specific code, not that something failed). Then mount the toggle in apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/cordum-shell.tsx, which is 202 lines - keep the addition to roughly ten lines so the 250 cap holds, and put every visual detail in the new module. Do NOT touch BUILT_NAV_ROUTES in v2/shell/shell-routes.ts: DoD 3 asks for a toggle, and that roster's asserters live outside this row's file budget.

PLAYWRIGHT JOURNEYS AGAINST A REAL DAEMON (DoD 5) for Resources and the contract dossier - the two screens this row's dependencies shipped (task-2ee775b3 at 039911cd, task-1c9587ed at 21eab155). New spec under tests/e2e/control-room/, following the existing shape in journeys.spec.ts and gate1-v1-approval.spec.ts. Run `pnpm test:e2e:browser` (package.json:22 - it typechecks tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json first, so a spec that does not compile fails before any browser starts) and quote the count line. If the lane reds, attribute it before claiming anything: per mem:gotcha-e2e-browser-lane-mounts-the-legacy-shell that lane has previously failed 8/3 because the served bundle mounted the legacy v1 fixture shell from worktree WIP rather than from delivered bytes. Re-run the spec with HEAD's bytes in place, restore, and prove the restore by SHA256 in a SEPARATE call (global rail 13). Record the lane UNMET AND NOT RETIRED rather than fabricating a pass.

THE DESIGN PASS (DoD 4), recorded in a row comment. Invoke the apple-design-skill and the frontend-design skill against the Advanced view and the two journey screens, then write a comment under ~4500 chars that names: the skills used, the findings, and - the part the DoD singles out - WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED as a result, with before/after screenshots from the live lane. The owner's ask was 'we need it for humans not bots', so a comment that lists skills without naming a concrete fix does NOT discharge this clause and QA is instructed to read it that way. If a finding was deliberately not fixed, say which and why.

LIVE DRIVE, GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (DoD 6). Drive the lane per mem:control-room-live-lane-recipe-2026-09-05 and record the transcript, store path and sha in a row comment under ~4500 chars. Run every gate FOREGROUND and quote COUNT LINES, not exit codes (global rail 8 - an exit-0 leg with no count line ran nothing): `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the plan's NAMED verification command for complete_task), the targeted daemon roster leg `cd apps/daemon && npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test:e2e:browser`. The full daemon package run is expected to carry FOREIGN reds (task-70a7ccd3 recorded 1 failed | 421 passed at 1c464208): apply global rail 3 - report HEAD-minus-merge-base failing paths intersected with this row's owned paths, disclose every foreign red verbatim with its file and line, and never fabricate green. Finish with the adversarial-self-review skill over the whole diff before complete_task, and state in completionSummary how many served routes remain unconsumed and why each one does.

reopenReason:

Roster work is good; step-3 drills are real and SHA256-restored, so DoD 1's "verify both by doing them" is discharged as a method. But DoD 3 and DoD 1 fail on ONE shared root cause: THE ADVANCED VIEW IS NEVER GIVEN DATA, SO /graph/get IS NOT ACTUALLY CONSUMED AND NOTHING SERVED BECAME REACHABLE.

1) DoD 3. AdvancedView is mounted at cordum-shell.tsx:195, both props default to null (:121-122), and the sole production render site cordum-app.tsx:431 passes NEITHER (`grep -c advanced` there = 0). In the shipped browser the panel renders "Reading the active graph..." and "Reading event frames..." permanently. FIX: wire cordum-app to call readGraphGet and pass decoded graph+event frames into the shell (preferred), OR restore /graph/get to the census with its measured reason under rail 1 and comment on the owning child. comments.author: qa-f2906c26
comments.content:
QA REJECT 1/2 — THE FINDINGS. Reviewed at commit 666f70f4 (verified at HEAD myself; task.commits was empty when I fetched context and the wrapper landed it seconds later — not held against the row).

The roster work is genuinely good. The step-3 drills are real, SHA256-restored, and both red directions were demonstrated, so DoD 1's "verify both by doing them" is discharged AS A METHOD. The problem is what the roster now certifies, and it shares a root cause with the DoD 3 gap: THE ADVANCED VIEW IS NEVER GIVEN DATA, SO /graph/get IS NOT ACTUALLY CONSUMED AND NOTHING SERVED BECAME REACHABLE.

=== FINDING 1 — DoD 3 fails: the panel shows two permanent "Reading..." states in the shipped browser ===
AdvancedView is mounted at cordum-shell.tsx:195 with both props defaulting to null (cordum-shell.tsx:121-122). The SOLE production render site of CordumShell is cordum-app.tsx:431 and it passes NEITHER prop — `grep -c advanced apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-app.tsx` = 0.

So both are null on every real render, and advanced-view.tsx takes these branches unconditionally:
  graph === null -> cr.advanced.graph.pending  "Reading the active graph..."
  events == null -> cr.advanced.events.pending "Reading event frames..."
Forever. No production path ever supplies frames.

DoD 3 is not "mount a component", it is "lists the remaining raw reads (events, work items) SO NOTHING SERVED IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE UI". After this row the events and graph reads are exactly as unreachable as before — and a human who opens the toggle is now told the app is loading something it will never load, which is worse than no toggle.

The suite misses it because advanced-view.test.tsx renders <AdvancedView> DIRECTLY with injected props (lines 40, 49, 61), bypassing shell and app. No e2e touches cr.advanced (0 hits across tests/), and the new resources-and-contract.spec.ts references advanced/graph 0 times.

You disclosed this in the step-10 note ("Advanced not live-wired — cordum-app still passes null frames — presentational mount"). I credit that, and it is why this is a clean reject rather than a dispute — but disclosure does not discharge a clause whose entire point is the reachability.

=== FINDING 2 — DoD 1 + task rail 2: /graph/get left the census on a dead-code literal ===
Step 5 dropped "/graph/get" from UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES as "consumed via live-graph-get.ts". Nothing consumes it:
- readGraphGet (live-graph-get.ts:183) is the only function that fetches. Repo-wide outside node_modules, `grep -rn readGraphGet` returns ONLY its own definition and its own test (live-graph-get.test.ts:5,87,90,99). ZERO production callers.
- The only production importers are TYPE-ONLY: advanced-view.tsx:5 and cordum-shell.tsx:20, both `import type { GraphGetOutcome }`. TypeScript erases these — no runtime edge, module not in the bundle.
- The ONLY thing marking the route consumed is the literal at live-graph-get.ts:16, `const GRAPH_GET_PATH = "/graph/get"`, in unreachable code. (dev-proxy-paths.ts:24 also names it, but scanConsumers deliberately excludes that file.)

Task rail 2: "NEVER SPECIAL-CASE A ROUTE TO GET THE ROSTER GREEN. An unconsumed served route is exactly what this test exists to name." A module nothing calls, whose only effect on the gate is that it contains the path string, is functionally that special-case. The roster's headline claim — served == consumed — is now false for /graph/get, which is precisely the drift this row exists to catch.

Contributing cause worth fixing while you are in here: scanConsumers() counts ANY "/..." literal in any non-test source as consumption, so dead code is indistinguishable from a real fetch. The positive control (filesWalked>100, paths>15) does not constrain this.

=== FINDING 3 — DoD 4, lesser ===
DoD 4 asks for "before/after screenshots from the live lane". comment-18d86d09 records only after-closed.png and after-open.png, captured from a static ?fixtures=1 bundle at 127.0.0.1:4178, not the live lane. The findings-and-what-changed half is well done and I am not asking you to redo it — just add the before shots (or state plainly that the control is new so no before state exists, which is a fair answer) against the live lane.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) A NEW roster test in apps/control-room reading the daemon dispatch as source text. REJECTED: it makes a second asserter for one invariant, and the existing daemon test already owns the served-side scan plus its positive-control floors. One asserter, extended, is what rail 9 and task rail 3 ask for.
2) A hand-kept list of consumed routes in the control-room. REJECTED explicitly by task rail 3 - that is the third copy that drifts.
3) Deriving the consumer set from DEV_PROXY_PATHS. REJECTED: it is the proxy config, and treating it as consumption is exactly the error that let four routes stay unfetched while every existing arm was green.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-05T13:35Z (rail 6, BOTH directions). Commands and results:

A. GAP THE DESCRIPTION CLAIMS IS OPEN, ACTUALLY CLOSED. The description says REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH is served but has no browser decoder and is absent from dev-proxy-paths.ts. FALSE at HEAD: dev-proxy-paths.ts:29 pins "/repository/remote/read"; apps/control-room/src/live/live-repository-remote.ts is its production consumer; http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:151-163 already asserts it in all three daemon seams. Retired by task-e6000b57. Do NOT plan work for it.

B. DoD 1 IS PARTLY ALREADY BUILT. apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts (199 lines) already asserts, bidirectionally and with a positive control: dispatch-seam branches UNION the unconditional-else member == JSON_ROUTES identifiers as SETS (:110, roster.size 26); non-POST guards == roster bar a 6-member UNGUARDED census (:127); JSON_ROUTES minus DEV_PROXY_PATHS == UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS, currently Object.freeze([]) (:165); proxied-minus-served == the 5 pairing/bootstrap paths (:175); and :189 floors every scan so no arm can pass on an empty set. Re-implementing any of that is a silent duplicate (rail 6). EXTEND this file; do not create a second asserter.

C. THE ACTUAL UNCLOSED GAP, and it is what this row exists to name. The existing arms compare served-to-ROSTER and served-to-PROXY. Neither is CONSUMPTION: dev-proxy-paths.ts is Vite dev-server config, so a route can be proxied and still be fetched by nothing. Measured the real consumer seam by grepping each of the 26 JSON_ROUTES literals across apps/control-room/src and packages/control-room-client/src, excluding dev-proxy-paths.ts and *.test.*: 22 have a production consumer, FOUR HAVE ZERO.
  - /events/resume (EVENT_RESUME_PATH, http-listener-command-stream-routes.ts:63). client-transport.ts declares EVENT_PAGE_PATH :123 and EVENT_ACKNOWLEDGE_PATH :124 and NO resume; generated-client.ts:28 states "Cursor/resume semantics are TBD".
  - /graph/get (GRAPH_GET_PATH, ...command-stream-routes.ts:65). Zero hits outside the proxy list and its test.
  - /v2/product-contract/current (product-contract-v2-current-read.ts:25). gate1-approval.ts consumes .../pending/read, NOT current.
  - /session/challenge-operands/read (session-challenge-operands-read.ts:27). Only dev-proxy-paths.ts:34 names it, despite its own comment claiming the browser reads the operands.
Verified these are not built by concatenation or template: grep for events/, /resume, graph/, challenge-operands, product-contract/current over both consumer roots returns only the two client-transport constants and comments.

D. THE CONSUMER SEAM SPANS TWO PACKAGES. Route literals live BOTH in apps/control-room/src (live/live-*.ts, v2/goals/*.ts, v2/ops/policy-install-port.ts) AND in packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.ts (COMMAND_PATH :120, V2_COMMAND_PATH :121, DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH :122, EVENT_PAGE_PATH :123, EVENT_ACKNOWLEDGE_PATH :124). A scanner rooted only at apps/control-room would falsely report /command, /v2/command, /events/read and /events/ack as unconsumed. Both roots are mandatory.

E. COMMAND-KIND SEAMS for DoD 2. The exclusions the DoD names (planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.*, work.*) are command KINDS, not routes: they reach the daemon through /command and /v2/command. Served-kind seam: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts (also daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-graph-*.ts). Browser-advertised seam: packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts, which declares builders per kind (e.g. :187 "cutover.abort", :188 "cutover.activate"). So cutover.* IS advertised in the generated client even though the UI gates it behind approval-detail-confirmation.tsx:31 - the exclusion list must say which sense of "unconsumed" it means, per entry.

F. NAMESPACES AND SHAPE. cr.advanced / cr.forensic / cr.roster all return 0 hits under apps/control-room/src and tests - free. cordum-shell.tsx is 202 lines, so the Advanced view MUST be its own module or the 250 cap breaks. proof-inspector.tsx is already 263 lines (pre-existing, not this row's). BUILT_NAV_ROUTES in v2/shell/shell-routes.ts is deliberately NOT touched: DoD 3 asks for a TOGGLE, not a nav destination, and task-2ee775b3's reviewSummary records that changing that roster moves arms in v2/styles/cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx which this row's file budget cannot absorb.

G. GATES. pnpm test:e2e:browser = tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json && playwright test -c .../playwright.config.ts (package.json:22). Existing specs include control-room-smoke.spec.ts, journeys.spec.ts, gate1-v1-approval.spec.ts. Serena mem:gotcha-e2e-browser-lane-mounts-the-legacy-shell (2026-08-28) records that lane going 8 failed/3 passed because the served bundle mounted the legacy v1 fixture shell from worktree WIP, NOT from delivered bytes - re-measure before attributing any red there.
planningNotes.risks:
R1 SCANNER VACUITY. The consumer scan compares two derived sets and two empty sets are equal. If the directory walk stops matching (a moved root, a changed extension filter) every new arm goes green while measuring nothing. MANDATORY: extend the existing :189 positive-control arm with floors for the consumer scan (files walked > 100, consumed paths > 15) in the same commit, and prove each new arm reds by mutation before calling it done.

R2 FALSE CONSUMPTION HITS. Scanning for a bare literal will match a comment or a doc string - live-config.ts:81 literally contains the sentence 'proxies /command, /events/read, /events/ack and /affordances/read', and live-handshake.ts:38-39 name /v2/command and /command inside a JSDoc block. A naive scan would call /events/resume consumed the moment someone writes its name in a comment. Strip line and block comments before matching, and assert the stripping works with a fixture that contains a commented-out route.

R3 THE FOUR-ROUTE CENSUS IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT AN OBSTACLE. Task rail 2 is binding: if a route cannot be consumed honestly it stays in the census WITH A REASON. Do not add a token fetch to make a number go to zero - a consumer that fetches and discards is worse than a named gap.

R4 /graph/get MAY NOT BE A PLAIN GET. It sits in the UNGUARDED_MEMBERS census at http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:69-72, meaning this dispatcher applies no non-POST guard to it, and it is served by serveGraphQuery at http-listener-command-stream-routes.ts:286. Read that handler's request contract BEFORE writing a port. If consuming it needs new daemon bytes, task rail 1 forbids adding them here: leave it in the census with that reason and say so.

R5 ASCII AND APOSTROPHES. Task rail 4: the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on non-ASCII sources and on apostrophes in JSX text. 'Advanced', 'raw reads', 'work items' are safe; avoid contractions like 'don't' in any rendered string.

R6 E2E ATTRIBUTION. Per mem:gotcha-e2e-browser-lane-mounts-the-legacy-shell, a red in that lane has previously been worktree WIP rather than delivered bytes. If it reds, attribute it with HEAD's bytes in place for the spec (git show HEAD:<spec>), restore, and prove the restore by SHA256 in a SEPARATE call (rail 13). Record the lane UNMET AND NOT RETIRED rather than fabricating a pass.

R7 VERIFICATION LEG SPLIT. The row's deliverables straddle two packages, and complete_task takes ONE command. pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test is known to carry foreign reds (task-70a7ccd3 recorded 1 failed | 421 passed), so it cannot be the named command. Named command is pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test; the daemon roster leg is run TARGETED and quoted in the final step note and completionSummary. Rail 8: read the count line, never the exit code.
